title: Goal Anchorboard — Q1 2026 Sprint Check-ins
content:
Purpose: lightweight personal anchorboard to keep focus on 3 outcome-level KPIs, weekly micro-checkins, and quick retrospective notes. Not polished — notes to self.

How I use this: every Monday morning update current numbers, every Friday 15min retro (what moved, blockers, micro-experiments). If something needs handoff, add the ticket/PR link below.

Top-level outcome KPIs (hypotheses):
- KPI A: 99th-percentile inference latency under 220ms for canonical chat route (p95 target already hit).
  - signal metric: daily 99th of production route / #requests at >=2s bucket.
  - current baseline (2026-03-10): 245ms (worse than target). Source: datadog/slo-dashboard.
  - quick thought: regression started ~2026-02-12 after kernel bump; suspect batching geometry change + small-model cache warmup.

- KPI B: cost per 1k tokens for our core hosted model reduced by 12% vs Jan baseline via batching + quantization picks.
  - signal metric: $/1k tokens over traffic sample window (3-day rolling).
  - current baseline: $0.78/1k tokens (target 0.69).
  - recent actions: ran experiment q8-quant-2 on dedicated pool, saw 9% saving but +6% tail latency.

- KPI C: rollout safety — automated canary detection false positive rate <2% (reduce noise so oncall trusts alerts).
  - signal: false positive rate (alerts that triggered manual rollback and later proven not needed).
  - baseline: 4.8% (too noisy).
  - action: refine threshold + add prompt-level quality check in rollouts.

Weekly micro-checkin entries (format: date — quick numbers / notes / blockers):

2026-03-10 — 99th latency 245ms / $/1k = 0.78 / FPR 4.2%\- Notes: kernel bump rollback candidate confirmed in staging replicates tail. Created JIRA-4821 to instrument per-batch size latency.\- Blockers: need infra window to run broad kernel rollback; chat with infra ops this Thurs.

2026-03-03 — 99th 238ms / $/1k = 0.79 / FPR 4.5%\- Notes: ran small-scale q8-quant-2; cost improved but tail got worse. Suspect interaction with caching TTL.\- Experiment: toggle cache-ttl from 30s->60s for 1% of traffic (A/B) — scheduled.

2026-02-24 — 99th 222ms / $/1k = 0.86 / FPR 5.1%\- Notes: great day — latency near target but cost spiked (burst traffic + cold VMs).\- Learn: need better autoscale headroom config.

Quick retrospective (rolling):
- Wins: small quantized build achieved near-target cost saving in isolated tests; canary pipeline now surfaces prompt-level regressions which helped avoid two bad rollouts.
- Losses: tail latency drifted after infra/kernel change; we were slow to correlate with batching geometry.
- Decisions: prioritize tail latency over marginal token cost for now (product OKR alignment).
- To experiment next: combined policy — q8-quant but with stricter batch size cap + sticky KV cache for hot sessions. Hypothesis: preserve tail while keeping 8% cost win.

TODOS / next steps (prioritized):
1) High: schedule infra rollback window + run A/B of kernel v3.14 vs v3.12 (owner: Marcus, ticket JIRA-4821).
2) High: launch cache-ttl A/B for 1% traffic, capture tail latency by session length buckets (owner: Aisha).\3) Medium: implement batch size cap toggle in-serving (feature flag) and run stress job 1h (owner: Marcus / infra).
4) Low: re-run quantized build with per-batch latency budget; collect cost vs tail tradeoff.

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Are we measuring tail correctly? double-check p99 vs 99th artifact math in our pipeline (sometimes p99 computed on 1m sample leading to aliasing).
- If rollback improves tail but cost jumps 4%, what's the product tradeoff? set explicit guardrails with product manager (Noah).
- Can we add a quick heatmap of batch-size vs latency in devtools? file a GH issue with perf logs attached.

Callouts / quick comms drafts (copy/paste ready):
- Channel note for infra ops: "Heads-up: requesting kernel rollback window Thurs 03/12 02:00-04:00 UTC to validate tail latency regressions — will patch canary and monitor. Ticket JIRA-4821."
- Slack DM to PM: "Noah — tail latency drift risks Q1 SLA. Proposed temporary rollbacks until combined quant+cap experiment proves stable. Can we align on acceptable token-cost delta?"

Handoff checklist (if I need to delegate):
- share JIRA-4821 with infra owner + attach staging perf results + steps to reproduce.\- ensure A/B run configs are in experiments repo (folder: experiments/anchorboard/q1).

Random brain-dump (keep for later):
- Idea: "focus tether" — a small dashboard tile showing top-3 tasks and one-week expected impact (delta on KPI). Helps avoid context switching.
- Could reuse rollout pipeline's existing metadata to attach expected KPI impact to each change.

End note: keep this lean. Move items that become docs to confluence and keep this anchored to quick updates only.

References:
- perf dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/slo-kpis\- experiments repo: https://github.com/redwood/experiments/tree/main/anchorboard/q1

— Marcus
